Chapter 8: Adapting the System as Children Grow
As kids get older, their understanding of money—and what they need from it—starts to change. The beauty of the three-jar system and the 3-6-5 approach is that they're designed to change right along with your child. This flexibility is what keeps money management interesting, practical, and actually fun as they move through different stages of life.
When children are young, it’s all about simple, hands-on actions—like sorting coins, picking a cause to support, or saving up for a small treat at the store. But as they grow, the system can grow, too. Imagine your child starting to save for something bigger, like a new bike or even a special trip. Suddenly, they’re thinking in months instead of weeks, learning patience and planning as they go.
Older kids and teens can take on even more. They might set up a basic budget, track where their money’s going—maybe with a simple spreadsheet or a handy app—and learn to juggle allowance, earnings, and expenses.
And what about earning? As kids become more independent, they might pick up small jobs or start a mini business—like mowing lawns or selling crafts—managing real income and making decisions about what to do with it.
The system can also shift to reflect what they care about most. If your child gets excited about environmental causes, for example, maybe more of their giving jar goes to support those organizations. Or, if your teen is thinking ahead to college, you could help them set up a separate savings account just for that big goal.
Here’s another powerful idea: let your kids help shape the rules. As they mature, invite them to decide how money gets divided, pick new ways to keep track, or come up with family giving projects. When they feel like they have a say, their motivation and engagement naturally grow.
Of course, mistakes and setbacks will happen. As kids take on more responsibility, they’ll make choices that don’t always work out—and that’s okay. In fact, those moments are some of the best learning opportunities. As a family, you can support each other by talking things through, offering advice, and celebrating the effort, not just the results.
So, here’s the key takeaway: the three-jar system and the 3-6-5 approach aren’t meant to stay the same forever. They’re living, breathing frameworks you can adapt to fit your child’s age, interests, and whatever life throws your way. By making these adjustments as your kids grow, you’ll help make sure that managing money stays meaningful, empowering, and effective—every step of the way.
